page.layout: One page of text in a single column; a woodcut ornament in the middle of the page; a catchword at the lower right. No margin notes.

main_text.p: Homines otiosi in locis suspectis habitare, & versari solent. Curc. 4. 1. v. 10. Vide Tit. Urbis Romae.
Ignaviae precia sunt verbera. Men. 5. 6. v. 11.
Ignavi milites mulieres dicti. Vide Tit. Mulier.
Ignavia ad omne vitium impellit adolescentes. Trin. 3. 2. v. 24, 29, 32.
Chrysost. πᾶσαν ἡσυχίαν ἐπιδἀξειν ἡ ἀργία.
Diem sermone terere, segnities mera est. Trin. 3. 3. v. 67.
Ignavia non secus ac tempestas adobruit juvenilem ætatem. Most. 1. 2. v. 56. & seqq. ἀλλὰ γοεικὰς.

p.i: Multa damna secum apportat huic ætati.

main_text.p: Pigri stimulis sunt fodiendi. Bacch. 5. 2. v. 40.

page.notes: The Greek in the entries after "Chrysost." and "Most. 1. 2. v. 56." is set in a Greek italic and is only approximately read. The woodcut ornament is not transcribed.
